title: Continuation Reduction Semantics
purpose: Define the meaning, objective, and constraints of continuation reduction before introducing concrete reduction rules.

canonical_claims.statement: Reduction is the process of transforming a well-formed continuation expression toward its canonical continuation form NF(C).

formal_objects.name: Continuation Reduction Semantics
formal_objects.definition: A governed reduction relation that transforms a well-formed continuation expression toward its canonical continuation form NF(C) while preserving process equivalence and leaving RT_core unchanged; it is not a symbolic rewrite operator.

laws.name: Reduction Preservation
laws.meaning: A lawful reduction step preserves process equivalence.

laws.name: Normalization Objective
laws.meaning: Lawful reduction aims at canonical continuation form when admissibility allows.

laws.name: Termination Neutrality
laws.formal: This patch does not assert that every continuation necessarily reaches NF(C).
laws.meaning: Reduction is defined without claiming universal termination.

laws.name: Semantic Preservation
laws.formal: Reduction preserves lawful continuation behavior and does not alter RT_core.
laws.meaning: Reduction changes representation, not the canonical core or governing behavior.

next_recommended_patch.title: Primitive Continuation Reduction Rules
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Introduce the first lawful reduction transformations that move continuation expressions toward NF(C).
